open: FUEL, not layout, is what kills the seeded opening now. Unattended from boot, the hearth and coal generator burn their starting coal and the whole grid starves around t=6000 (supply 16 vs demand 96) — every building on it then freezes, correctly. The opening places no scrap_collector and no ore_drill, so there is no coal income at all until the player builds one. This is pre-existing (the E5 probe already showed hearth fuel at 2.14 and falling at t=6000) and it is [P03]/[P04]/[P12]'s call whether the opening should ship with a coal source or whether running dry in five minutes IS the first lesson. My freeze test is explicitly conditional on the grid being solvent and asserts separately that it IS solvent at t=600/2000/4000, so it cannot pass vacuously when someone fixes this.

I deliberately did NOT add must_connect=['heat'] to turret_mount/watchtower, which would make the BUILD SYSTEM refuse a defensive building placed off the grid the way it already refuses a warmth_radiator. Two reasons: seven committed scenarios place turrets and watchtowers at coordinates tools/gen_scenarios.py generated under the old rules, and refusing the placement takes away the exact failure the ATTENTION stack and the WARMTH lens exist to diagnose (Factorio lets you place the turret; it just does not work). If the integrator wants the harder rule, the experiment is one line per .tres plus a run of tests/p00/test_scenarios.gd.

The climate offset moves EVERY sim tick 2016 ticks later on the world clock. Anything that hard-codes 'tick N is phase P' outside game/sim/climate/ is now wrong by that much. ClimateSystem.clock_tick() is public for exactly this. I grepped and fixed the only consumer I own (the climate suite); [P08] threat reads climate through its own API and its 2498 assertions still pass, but [P12]/[P20] should check any tick-to-phase arithmetic of their own.

Day 1 is shorter: 216 s of daylight before nightfall instead of 316.8 s. Night is unchanged at 163.2 s, so day 1 still gives more time to build than to survive. If that is too tight for onboarding, ClimateProfile.opening_tick is the one number to move and the luminance sweep above is the cost of moving it.

[P13]: the join is still slightly out of true. PHASE_ARC maps the START of the sim's dawn phase onto palette 0.235, which is 59% of the way from the night keyframe to the dawn keyframe — so the first 336 ticks of every 'Dawn' are painted mostly as night, on day 2 and every day after. I moved where a run BEGINS because that is what I own; the durable fix is a palette keyframe at ~0.235 named dawn, or PHASE_ARC starting dawn at 0.27. Same for the sun: ClimateProfile.sun_at peaks at day progress 0.44 (tick 4224) while the palette's noon sits at PHASE_ARC 0.50 = tick 3072, so the brightest grade and the highest sun are 1150 ticks apart.

--ui-tour boots a real session and then sits at t000001 rendering frames without advancing the sim; it wrote no shots in the ten minutes I gave it. Not touched by anything I changed (the reachability suite boots the same path and passes in seconds), but somebody owns that.
